what-software-and-applications-are.caption: Every app on this phone is software: instructions a computer follows to do a job for someone
Left: the processor and memory live on circuit boards like this one, doing the work while the power is on
Each feature is a vertical slice through the interface, the logic and the data

different-types-of-applications.caption: The same software can reach people on a laptop, a tablet and a phone, each with different strengths
A mobile app installed on the device can use phone features such as location and notifications, and must be updated through an app store
A command-line program at work: no buttons or windows, just text commands and text output

from-a-problem-to-application-requiremen.caption: Requirements start as scattered ideas; your job is to turn them into a clear, agreed list
The best requirements start with a conversation
Teams often map journeys with sticky notes: one note per step, arranged left to right, so missing steps and unnecessary features are easy to spot

the-software-development-lifecycle.caption: Building software is a team activity that moves through planning, building, testing and release
Some people read screens through a braille display or a screen reader rather than by sight
On a team, the lifecycle is shared between many people

turning-requirements-into-a-design.caption: Design is where requirements become sketches of screens, parts and how they connect

application-architecture-and-boundaries.caption: Like a steel frame, architecture is the structure that holds everything else up

choosing-languages-frameworks-and-servic.caption: Languages, frameworks and services are tools: pick the box that fits the job

designing-data-and-integrations.caption: Data flows between parts of a system like water through pipes, and every joint is an integration

designing-for-quality-and-future-change.caption: Quality and future change are decided while the frame is still going up

understanding-ai-coding-tools.caption: AI coding tools are powerful helpers, but a human still decides what they should do

building-features-in-small-increments.caption: Big features are built from many small pieces, added one at a time

understanding-and-reviewing-generated-co.caption: Read generated code closely before you accept it

testing-and-verifying-behaviour.caption: Tests are small, careful experiments that prove the software behaves as expected

understanding-deployment-and-hosting.caption: Hosting means renting space on computers in a data centre that run your app all day

preparing-and-releasing-an-application.caption: A release checklist makes sure nothing important is forgotten before going live

observing-an-application-in-production.caption: Monitoring is your control room: it shows how the app is doing in production

protecting-data-and-recovering-from-fail.caption: Backups and recovery plans are a lifebuoy for when things go wrong

the-frontend-and-user-interface.caption: The frontend begins as sketches of the screens people will use

Backend code runs on servers like these, often in a data centre

modelling-and-working-with-data.caption: Modelling data means deciding what things exist and how they relate before you build
